claim: ADP's NER Pulse reported that, for the four weeks ending November 7, 2026, U.S. private employers added an average of 21,000 jobs per week. This is a timely private-sector employment indicator, not the BLS total nonfarm payroll first-print figure; it should be treated as contextual evidence only and not as a direct measurement of the market's +90,000 threshold.
quote: For the four weeks ending November 7, 2026, U.S. private employers added an average of 21,000 jobs per week, according to the NER Pulse, a weekly update of the monthly ADP National Employment Report (NER).
resolutionMapping: The market resolves on the BLS November 2026 first-print total nonfarm payroll change being at least +90,000. ADP NER Pulse is an independent, high-frequency private-sector payroll indicator and can inform the labour-market context before the BLS release, but it excludes public-sector employment, uses a four-week average ending November 7, is preliminary, and is not the BLS metric. It cannot alone establish whether the threshold is met.
verificationNote: User explicitly approved submission of this exact ADP NER Pulse evidence item after reviewing the claim, source, publication time, novelty boundary, and its limitation as contextual private-sector evidence rather than the BLS NFP measure.
